newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria revives delayed wheat purchase tender.
newsitem.headline: Algeria revives delayed wheat purchase tender.

text.p: Algeria has relaunched a previously postponed import tender for 75,000 tonnes of April/May wheat, grain traders said on Tuesday.
The tender was originally in the market last week but was postponed on Friday.
The tender is for wheat of optional origin, traders said.
It was not immediately clear whether French companies, who were reported to be barred from the previous tender, had been invited to offer wheat this time round.
Last week French firms said they had not been asked to take part in the tender, a move which many saw as possible evidence of new tensions over remarks made by France's prime minister.

Algeria's official press agency last week accused Prime Minister Alain Juppe of interfering in its affairs after he called for a "true democratic conscience" to be established in France's violence-racked former colony.
Although French firms were not involved in the original tender, it was widely assumed that Algeria would consider buying French wheat from foreign companies, traders said last week.
